lines: Scheduled for right radical nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma

On the day of surgery, the patient is brought to the operating room and placed under general anesthesia.
The surgical team performs a time-out procedure.
The circulating nurse confirms the patient's identity using the wristband and the medical record, and the surgeon confirms the procedure and the operative site.
The anesthesiologist reviews the patient's allergies and medication list.
Just before the first incision, the scrub nurse initiates a final time-out.

encounters.cc: Progressive lethargy and mild shortness of breath 48 hours after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair

lines: Progressive lethargy and mild shortness of breath 48 hours after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair

The patient is a 69-year-old male with a history of pancreatic adenocarcinoma status post pancreaticoduodenectomy, renal cell carcinoma status post right radical nephrectomy, and Stage IV colorectal adenocarcinoma who presents 48 hours after undergoing abdominal aortic aneurysm repair.
During the procedure, he has a significant drop in blood pressure that requires vasopressor support for stabilization.
Postoperatively, he is initially stable but develops progressive lethargy and mild shortness of breath over the next 48 hours.
His blood pressure remains low-normal despite fluid administration, and his skin appears cool.
Nursing staff note that his urine output has steadily decreased over the past day.

lines: Acute onset of lower extremity weakness, numbness, and urinary retention 12 hours after thoracic aortic aneurysm repair

The patient is a 70-year-old male with extensive vascular history including prior endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and cervical spondylosis who presents to the emergency department 12 hours following thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
He reports that he was initially able to move his legs postoperatively, but over the past few hours, he has lost the ability to move them.
He also complains of numbness in his legs and an inability to feel when his bladder is full.
